title: Providing paediatric emergency care to children
description: Recognise and manage paediatric emergencies, including anaphylaxis, seizures, shock and respiratory distress.
descriptors: 1.1 Manage paediatric patients requiring resuscitation
1.2 Provide initial evaluation and management of an acutely ill or injured paediatric patient
1.3 Formulate and implement a diagnostic and therapeutic plan for common paediatric emergencies
1.4 Perform common emergency procedures
1.5 Use point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) in emergency care
assessment: Information sources The standard set applies to this EPA — see "Standard assessment information sources" on page 8.
frequency: Six per annum Summative entrustment decision taken by Clinical Competency Committee WBA tools to use DOPS: observe registrars performing procedures in emergency and acute care units to assess technical skill, patient interaction and adherence to safety protocols. Mini-CEX: observe registrars during real-life critical care scenarios, such as resuscitation or complex patient management, and provide immediate feedback. CCA: review clinical notes and discuss cases involving critically ill children, focusing on clinical reasoning, decision-making and management plans. CBD: conduct structured discussions on recent cases managed by the trainee, exploring clinical reasoning and decision-making in depth. MSF: collect feedback from a range of colleagues, including nurses, other doctors and allied health professionals, as well as from patients' families, to assess interpersonal skills and professional behaviour. Clinical audit: audit specific aspects of paediatric emergency care, such as infection control practices or adherence to resuscitation protocols, to promote self-reflection and quality improvement. Reflective exercise: reflect on challenging cases or critical incidents, discussing experiences and learning points with a mentor or supervisor.

title: Managing common paediatric presentations
description: This EPA focuses on diagnosing and treating common paediatric presentations, such as respiratory infections, gastroenteritis, skin infections, and other ambulatory presentations prevalent in the South African context. Trainees must demonstrate proficiency in the assessment, diagnosis and management of these presentations in both outpatient and inpatient settings.
descriptors: 2.1 Diagnose common paediatric presentations
2.2 Present and discuss the differential diagnoses of children with a common condition
2.3 Perform procedures related to common presentations
2.4 Apply safe prescribing in the management of children with common presentations
2.5 Monitor a common condition according to severity and escalate care appropriately
2.6 Apply antimicrobial stewardship in the management of children with acute illness
2.7 Apply fluid and nutritional management in children with acute illness
2.8 Execute an appropriate discharge and follow-up plan
assessment: Information sources The standard set applies to this EPA — see “Standard assessment information sources” on page 8.
frequency: Six per annum Summative entrustment decision taken by Clinical Competency Committee (multiple staff members) WBA tools to use Mini-CEX: focused on acute assessment and decision-making, including the daily review of an admitted patient. CBD: for diagnostic reasoning and therapeutic decision-making, including cases in which the patient failed to progress or deteriorated on the ward. DOPS: phlebotomy, lumbar puncture, nebulisation. Direct observation: of a ward round led by the trainee, and of shift handover. CCA: structured review of the trainee’s own admission notes, daily progress notes and discharge summaries against the institutional standard. Chart-stimulated recall: questioning based on the trainee’s own records, to probe the reasoning behind documented ward decisions. MSF: from nursing staff, patients and peers, on professionalism and communication. RCA: review of clinical notes and outcomes in acute admissions. Clinical audit: of an aspect of ward care such as prescribing accuracy, early-warning-score compliance or discharge summary completeness.

title: Providing intensive care to children
description: This EPA focuses on the care of critically ill or injured children in the paediatric intensive care unit (PICU). The registrar must promptly recognise a child who requires intensive care because of a deteriorating condition or a life-threatening emergency, lead life-saving procedures, manage ventilated patients and coordinate a large team during emergencies.
descriptors: 3.1 Manage the resuscitation of a child in an intensive care unit
3.2 Manage a new patient admission to the PICU
3.3 Manage the ongoing care of patients in a PICU
3.4 Manage complications in patients in a PICU
3.5 Perform the procedures required in a PICU
3.6 Manage the referral of children from a PICU to a general care unit or institution
assessment: Information sources The standard set applies to this EPA — see "Standard assessment information sources" on page 8.
frequency: Six per annum Summative entrustment decision taken by Clinical Competency Committee (multiple staff members) WBA tools to use Mini-CEX: observe registrars during real-life critical care scenarios, such as resuscitation or complex patient management, and provide immediate feedback. CCA: review clinical notes and discuss cases involving critically ill children, focusing on clinical reasoning, decision-making and management plans. CBD: conduct structured discussions on recent cases managed by the trainee, exploring clinical reasoning and decision-making in depth. MSF: collect feedback from a range of colleagues, including nurses, other doctors and allied health professionals, as well as from patients' families, to assess interpersonal skills and professional behaviour. RCA: select cases at random from the registrar's patient records to identify knowledge gaps and areas for improvement. DOPS: observe registrars performing intensive care procedures to assess technical skill, patient interaction and adherence to safety protocols. Clinical audit: audit specific aspects of paediatric critical care, such as infection control practices or adherence to resuscitation protocols. Reflective exercise: reflect on challenging cases or critical incidents, discussing experiences and learning points with a mentor or supervisor.

title: Managing common neonatal conditions
description: This EPA focuses on the care of the newborn in the labour ward, the postnatal ward, the kangaroo mother care unit, the Level 1 nursery and the newborn follow-up visit. The registrar must examine the newborn, recognise and treat the conditions commonly encountered in the first days and weeks of life, establish safe feeding, thermal care and growth, lead resuscitation at delivery, and identify the baby whose needs exceed Level 1 care and arrange timely referral. The care of neonates requiring high-care or intensive care is covered by EPA 5.
descriptors: 4.1 Perform and document the routine examination of the newborn
4.2 Provide resuscitation and immediate care of the newborn at delivery
4.3 Manage the common conditions of the newborn in a Level 1 setting
4.4 Establish feeding, thermal care and growth, including kangaroo mother care
4.5 Perform the core procedures of newborn care
4.6 Recognise the newborn who is deteriorating and refer for a higher level of care
4.7 Communicate with and counsel the caregivers of a newborn
4.8 Execute an appropriate discharge, immunisation and follow-up plan
assessment: Information sources The standard set applies to this EPA — see “Standard assessment information sources” on page 8.
frequency: Six per annum Summative entrustment decision taken by Neonatal team Clinical Competency Committee (multiple staff members) WBA tools to use Mini-CEX CBD DOPS CCA, applied to the newborn clinical record, the discharge summary and the referral letter. Direct observation of handover and of caregiver counselling. MSF, with contributions from neonatal nurses or midwives, medical officers and interns, allied health professionals (for example, dietitians and lactation advisors), and consultant paediatricians. MSF responses must reflect meaningful clinical interaction and be coordinated by the supervising consultant. Results must be collated, summarised and discussed with the trainee.

title: Providing neonatal care in intensive and high-care settings
description: This EPA focuses on the care of very sick, small or premature newborns in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) and the neonatal high-care unit. The registrar must promptly recognise a deteriorating neonate, perform life-saving procedures, manage respiratory and feeding support, and lead neonatal resuscitation.
descriptors: 5.1 Provide neonatal resuscitation
5.2 Manage preterm neonates
5.3 Manage complex neonates
5.4 Perform core neonatal procedures
5.5 Manage the referral of neonates with complex presentations
5.6 Manage the transport of neonates with complex presentations
5.7 Manage the long-term follow-up of complex neonatal patients
assessment: Information sources The standard set applies to this EPA — see "Standard assessment information sources" on page 8.
frequency: Six per annum Summative entrustment decision taken by Neonatal team Clinical Competency Committee (multiple staff members) WBA tools to use CBD DOPS MSF, with contributions from neonatal nurses or midwives, medical officers and interns, allied health professionals (for example, dietitians and physiotherapists), and consultant neonatologists or paediatricians. MSF responses must reflect meaningful clinical interaction and be coordinated by the supervising consultant. Results must be collated, summarised and discussed with the trainee.

title: Managing long-term health conditions (LTHCs)
description: This EPA focuses on the comprehensive care of children living with Long-term health conditions and chronic illness.
descriptors: 6.1 Manage a patient with a long-term health condition, including clinical assessment, investigation and management
6.2 Perform procedures on patients with LTHCs
6.3 Develop and implement a multi-disciplinary plan to manage a child with a LTHC
6.4 Present patients with LTHCs at a clinical or academic meeting
assessment: Information sources The standard set applies to this EPA — see "Standard assessment information sources" on page 8.
frequency: Four per annum Summative entrustment decision taken by Clinical Competency Committee (multiple staff members) WBA tools to use Direct observation (clinical) Mini-CEX (clinical case) DOPS Case note review MSF

title: Maintaining and promoting the health and well-being of children
description: This EPA focuses on promoting children's health and development at every stage so that they can live healthy lives and reach their full potential. Preventing mortality and morbidity through preventive medicine, such as immunisation, is central to this activity.
descriptors: 7.1 Perform well-baby checks
7.2 Perform developmental and growth screening
7.3 Administer vaccinations to infants
7.4 Evaluate and complete the Road to Health booklet
assessment: Information sources The standard set applies to this EPA — see "Standard assessment information sources" on page 8.
frequency: Two per annum Summative entrustment decision taken by Clinical Competency Committee (multiple staff members) WBA tools to use Mini-CEX: for example, a clinical scenario forming part of teaching rounds. DOPS: directly observed administration of vaccinations, Mantoux testing and similar procedures. Directly observed clinical examination: well-baby and well-child examinations. MSF: feedback from multidisciplinary teams and outreach hospitals and clinics, supported by discharge summaries and outpatient clinic notes documenting the problems identified and addressed.

title: Evaluating and managing neurodevelopmental and behavioural presentations in children
description: This EPA focuses on identifying, assessing and supporting children with developmental delay or behavioural differences, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), cerebral palsy, global developmental delay and learning difficulties.
descriptors: 8.1 Conduct a developmental and behavioural assessment
8.2 Formulate a differential diagnosis and an initial management plan for a child with a neurodevelopmental condition
8.3 Coordinate multidisciplinary care for children with neurodevelopmental presentations
assessment: Assessment requirements are set to be achievable while ensuring adequate exposure. Progression aligns with overall competency development across the four-year training period, and flexibility is built in for local context and resource availability. Information sources The standard set applies to this EPA — see "Standard assessment information sources" on page 8.
frequency: One per annum Summative entrustment decision taken by Clinical Competency Committee (multiple staff members) WBA tools to use Mini-CEX DOPS CBD MSF Reflective exercise

title: Providing care for an adolescent patient
description: This EPA focuses on meeting the distinct physical, emotional, and social health needs of adolescent patients (the second decade of life). This EPA includes screening for risk behaviour, managing confidentiality, and supporting the patient to take responsibility for their own health decisions.
descriptors: 9.1 Manage acute presentations in adolescent patients
9.2 Manage an adolescent with long-term health conditions
9.3 Develop a plan for the transition of a patient with an LTHC into adult care
assessment: Information sources The standard set applies to this EPA — see "Standard assessment information sources" on page 8.
frequency: One per annum Summative entrustment decision taken by Clinical Competency Committee (multiple staff members) WBA tools to use Direct observation CBD MSF

title: Leading and operating within a clinical team
description: This EPA involves demonstrating effective clinical leadership in a paediatric healthcare setting. The trainee is expected to lead a multidisciplinary team, manage clinical operations and ensure high-quality patient care. This includes decision-making, communication and conflict resolution.
descriptors: 10.1 Prioritise tasks and manage time efficiently while on call
10.2 Facilitate effective handover to other healthcare providers
10.3 Collaborate effectively with interprofessional team members to ensure comprehensive patient care
10.4 Coordinate patient discharge plans
10.5 Conduct a clinical audit
10.6 Complete a patient safety incident report
10.7 Participate in a quality improvement project
assessment: Information sources The standard set applies to this EPA — see "Standard assessment information sources" on page 8.
frequency: Six per annum Summative entrustment decision taken by Clinical Competency Committee (multiple staff members) WBA tools to use MSF Direct observation

title: Managing population health challenges
description: Advocate effectively for, and coordinate interventions in, paediatric community-based care, healthcare policy and intersectoral collaboration.
descriptors: 11.1 Coordinate a mortality and morbidity meeting
11.2 Present health statistics at a meeting
11.3 Compile a quality referral to community-based or multisectoral stakeholders
assessment: Information sources The standard set applies to this EPA — see "Standard assessment information sources" on page 8.
frequency: One per annum Summative entrustment decision taken by Clinical Competency Committee (multiple staff members) WBA tools to use MSF CBD Direct observation

title: Communicating with and counselling patients, caregivers and healthcare teams
description: This EPA focuses on sharing clear health information with patients and their families, and with colleagues across the healthcare team. The registrar must convey medical information in an easy-to-understand way, listen well, and work effectively as a team member.
descriptors: 12.1 Communicate effectively with patients and families in emergency settings
12.2 Communicate effectively with patients and families in the neonatal ICU, neonatal high care and PICU
12.3 Counsel caregivers about immunisation, growth charts and dysmorphism
12.4 Demonstrate counselling for common presentations
12.5 Lead a counselling session with the family of a child with an LTHC
12.6 Demonstrate counselling in palliative care scenarios
12.7 Communicate effectively with healthcare colleagues
assessment: Information sources The standard set applies to this EPA — see "Standard assessment information sources" on page 8.
frequency: Six per annum Summative entrustment decision taken by Clinical Competency Committee (multiple staff members) WBA tools to use Mini-CEX MSF CBD Chart-stimulated recall

title: Managing child protection, legal and ethical aspects of children at risk
description: This EPA focuses on the skills required to manage child protection cases effectively, including the legal, ethical and multidisciplinary aspects of safeguarding at-risk children.
descriptors: 13.1 Assess and document the signs of abuse or neglect
13.2 Complete a report of suspected child abuse
13.3 Refer to social and legal services (Child Protection Unit)
assessment: Information sources The standard set applies to this EPA — see "Standard assessment information sources" on page 8.
frequency: One per annum Summative entrustment decision taken by Clinical Competency Committee (multiple staff members) WBA tools to use MSF: feedback from multidisciplinary team members on the trainee's contribution to child protection cases, together with evaluation of the medical and legal documentation prepared by the trainee. Direct observation: observation of the trainee's interactions with at-risk children, families and multidisciplinary teams. CBD: detailed case discussions to evaluate decision-making, ethical reasoning and the handling of sensitive child protection situations. Mini-CEX: assessment of clinical examination skills, specifically in recognising the signs of abuse or neglect and performing a thorough child welfare assessment.

title: Providing palliative and end-of-life care
description: Support children by focusing on comfort, pain management, and emotional support for both the patient and their family.
descriptors: 14.1 Provide consultation for children requiring a palliative care approach
14.2 Draw up an advance care plan
14.3 Use appropriate pain management strategies in paediatric cases
14.4 Participate in the certification of brain death
assessment: Assessment requirements are set to be achievable while ensuring adequate exposure. Progression aligns with overall competency development throughout the four-year training period, and flexibility is built in to accommodate local context and resource availability. Information sources The standard set applies to this EPA — see "Standard assessment information sources" on page 8.
frequency: One per annum Summative entrustment decision taken by Clinical Competency Committee (multiple staff members) WBA tools to use MSF Reflective exercise CBD

title: Teaching and applying evidence-based care responsibly and ethically in clinical decision-making and research
description: This EPA covers the registrar's ability to teach and to practise evidence-based paediatrics ethically. They teach medical students, junior trainees, the interprofessional team and caregivers, adapting content and language to the learner. They formulate clinical questions, appraise the literature, and apply the evidence to the patient in front of them. Both carry ethical obligations to the patient whose case is used, to the learner, and to the integrity of the evidence. Artificial intelligence is used transparently and with verification, and never as a substitute for the registrar's own clinical reasoning.
descriptors: 15.1 Plan and deliver a structured teaching session for medical students or junior trainees
15.2 Provide teaching within the interprofessional team during ward rounds, handover or debriefing
15.3 Deliver caregiver or community education appropriate to the context and health literacy
15.4 Formulate a clinical question, appraise the literature, and present the evidence at a journal club or clinical meeting
15.5 Apply ethical principles in teaching and in evidence-based practice, including the responsible use of AI tools
15.6 Give and receive constructive feedback, and demonstrate reflective practice
assessment: Information sources The standard set applies (page 8) together with structured feedback from learners.
frequency: Once every six months, with an annual entrustment decision Feedback from at least two assessors across at least two teaching contexts, before entrustment is granted. Summative entrustment decision taken by Clinical Competency Committee (multiple staff members) WBA tools to use Direct observation: of a teaching session or caregiver education encounter, including how consent and privacy were handled. CBD: evidence-based decision-making on a real case, including how sources and any AI-supported information were appraised. Learner feedback: structured evaluation by students, junior trainees and team members taught by the registrar. MSF: on professionalism, inclusivity and honesty in teaching. Portfolio and logbook review: teaching sessions, journal club presentations, feedback received, and reflective entries.
